subject: Urgent: morning API spin‑up causing p95/p99 regressions — FinPay escalation
messages:
From: Sofia Duarte <sofia.duarte@finpay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: FinPay Engineering <eng@finpay.com>
Date: 2028-01-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Morning regressions — urgent

Marcus —

We started getting a bunch of 1xx+ ms spikes this morning around 08:45 PST (p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~2.4s, p99 to ~6.1s) right when our billing window opened. Traffic pattern didn't change on our side. Attaching a short trace and a screenshot of the dashboard. Can you confirm whether this was an incident on Redwood's side or something in our integration? This is impacting real transactions.

Attachment: finpay-trace-20280115.txt (log excerpt)
Attachment: latency-screenshot-20280115.png

— Sofia
Sofia Duarte
Head of Platform
FinPay
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-15T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Morning regressions — urgent

Thanks for the trace, Sofia — sorry you hit this. I’m opening a dedicated ticket and looping in engineering and support to triage immediately. Initial ask: could you confirm whether the affected requests all use the same model/route and whether you saw an increase in concurrency during the 08:40–09:00 window?

I’ll get back with findings within 90 minutes. We’ll keep you updated in this thread.

— Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-15T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Morning regressions — urgent

Marcus / Marissa —

I pulled the autoscaler and instance logs for the FinPay pool. Short summary: at 08:38 PST we saw a rapid ramp of requests that triggered the GPU pool autoscaler to provision 6 additional instances. Several of the new instances hit the service 'ready' probe but then stalled during CUDA/init and model JIT steps — root cause looks like concurrent nvml/cuInit contention during parallel instance spin-ups. That caused a brief backlog where a subset of frontends fell back to higher-latency routing leading to p95/p99 spike.

Mitigation we can push now (no deploy required): 1) temporary limit on parallel instance spin (autoscaler config) to stagger starts, 2) enable our pre-warm kernel path for the FinPay route to skip the heavy JIT step. Both low-risk; I can apply them within the hour.

I’ll open INF-9823 and attach logs. If we do the stagger change, there will be a short warm-up tail but it should flatten the p99s.

— Naomi Feldman
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Duarte <sofia.duarte@finpay.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-15T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Morning regressions — urgent

Sofia —

Thanks Naomi — that aligns with what we’re seeing. Naomi is going to apply two targeted changes (staggered spin policy + route-level pre-warm) and monitor. We expect measurable p95/p99 improvements within ~30–45 minutes after changes take effect.

We’re treating this as a high-priority incident. If FinPay prefers, we can also schedule a short maintenance window to pre-warm an extra standby node each morning for the billing ramp. Would you like us to enable that proactively while we finalize a long-term fix?

— Marcus
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Duarte <sofia.duarte@finpay.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-15T11:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Morning regressions — urgent

Looping in ops & CS notes: we applied staggered spin (max concurrent spin = 2) at 10:05 and enabled the route pre-warm at 10:12. Early telemetry: p95 dropped to ~210ms and p99 to ~840ms for the FinPay route within 20 minutes. We’ll keep a 6‑hour elevated monitoring window and follow up with a postmortem.

Sofia — apologies for the disruption. As a gesture while we complete the mitigation work, I’d like to offer a credit for the impacted billing period; Rishi, are you OK to approve a one-time credit up to $12k (account-level) if the postmortem shows this was on our side?

— Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-18T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Morning regressions — urgent

Marissa — approved. Please process the $12,000 service credit pending the postmortem. Also, Naomi: prioritize the longer-term fix (pre-provisioned standby node + improving concurrent init paths) and include ETA in INF-9823. I want a short exec note for our SLT summarizing cause, impact (est. % of requests affected), mitigation, and next steps by EOD tomorrow.

— Rishi Malhotra
VP, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
